claims.claim: No test files were added. Scenarios S3, S4, S5, S6, S7, S8, S10, S11, S12 and S13 each need an assertion-bearing test.
claims.accuracy_evidence: The BASE PATCH changes only exceptions.py, tree.py, ucd.py, check.py, iterparser.py and validate.py. It adds no test file. One caveat: BASE FAILURES lists an existing test_vo.py::TestParse::test_repr, so repr coverage may partly exist.
claims.addressed_evidence: X adds tests for all ten: collision, meta round-trip, get_ref and its KeyError, iter_values, get_values_by_id, VOTableFile repr, skipping empty tables, IndexError, and TableElement str/bytes/repr. Y changes no test files.

claims.claim: test_table.py::test_empty_table calls to_table() and ignores the result. It cannot check len==0 or colnames for S9.
claims.accuracy_evidence: In the referenced source, test_empty_table ends with a bare `table.to_table()` and has no assertion. The BASE PATCH does not change it.
claims.addressed_evidence: X now asserts `len(astropy_table) == 0` and `colnames == ["unsignedByte", "short"]`. Y leaves the test untouched.

claims.claim: UCDWords.__init__ ignores the word-type column and puts every word in both _primary and _secondary, so position checks never fire.
claims.accuracy_evidence: In the BASE ucd.py, the loop reads `type` but always calls both `self._primary.add(name_lower)` and `self._secondary.add(name_lower)`. A comment justifies this.
claims.addressed_evidence: X only adds to primary when type != "S", and only adds to secondary when type != "P". Y uses `type in "PQVCE"` for primary and `type in "SQVCE"` for secondary. Both now respect the type column.

claims.claim: Add a test that fails when a secondary-only UCD word is used as the primary word with check_controlled_vocabulary=True.
claims.accuracy_evidence: The BASE PATCH adds no ucd test. The inputs don't show whether the existing test_ucd.py already covers primary/secondary position checks.
claims.addressed_evidence: Neither X nor Y adds a UCD test. The claim is unverifiable, so this is N_A.

failure_clusters.evidence: Read individually, `check.py`, `iterparser.py`, `validate.py`, and `exceptions.py`'s restorations look correct
